## Context / Problem

The `[non-codebase]` acceptance-criterion exemption is silently inert when the tag is written in backticks, and rebar's own guidance text renders the tag in backticks. Authors who backtick the tag (the ordinary markdown instinct, and the form that does not read as a second empty checkbox) get a criterion that looks exempt, reviews as exempt, and is refused at close.

The canonical matcher is `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py:48-51`:

```python
r"^\s*-\s*\[[ xX]?\]\s*\[(?:non-codebase|operator-attested)\]\s*(.+?)\s*$"
```

It requires the tag as a bare bracketed literal immediately after the checkbox. Measured by importing it: the bare form matches; the backticked form does NOT match for `- [ ]`, for `- [x]`, and for the `[operator-attested]` alias alike.

Every deterministic parser of the tag imports that one matcher (or its sibling start-anchored pattern in the same module), so each is affected:

- Close precheck: `ensure_ac_boxes_checked` (`src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:504-542`) filters unchecked lines through it at `txn.py:528`, so a backticked tag exempts nothing and the close is refused.
- Attested-item validity at close: `ensure_attested_items_valid` (`txn.py:564-621`) calls `det_attestation_launder.laundering_gaps` (matcher use at `det_attestation_launder.py:111`) and `det_measurement_provenance.provenance_gaps` (matcher use at `det_measurement_provenance.py:136`). A backticked item is skipped by both, so a TICKED backticked `[non-codebase]` box is treated as an ordinary criterion: its `provenance:` requirement and the laundering check are silently skipped.
- Plan-review DET checks in `det_operator_attested.py`: `operator_evidence_ac_gaps` (`:158`) does not treat a backticked item as tagged, and `misplaced_tag_lines` (`:196-205`) uses `_TAG_AT_START_RE` (`:190-192`) plus code-span stripping (`_CODE_SPAN_RE`, `:193`), so a backticked tag at the start is neither honoured nor reported as misplaced.
- Pass-3 enrichment: `decide_ops.operator_attested_ac_texts` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/decide_ops.py:30-35`) calls `.findall()` on the same matcher, so a backticked criterion's in-session unverifiability is not recognised as by design.
- LLM classification: the completion-verifier prompt (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md:92-94`) and the evidence-kind reviewer prompt (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_evidence_kind.md:55-58`) tell the model the tag must be exact at the start of the checkbox text, without saying whether a backticked tag counts.

Observed cost: the close of `f10f-c24a-3cfa-449e` failed (RC=1) on 2026-11-02 on exactly this, after its change had merged; recovery requires a material description edit and a fresh `review-plan`.

## Approach

Widen the accepted surface (decided in this ticket; narrowing the guidance instead would leave already-written descriptions broken). In `det_operator_attested.py`, define the accepted tag form once as a non-capturing alternation of the bare tag and the same tag wrapped in a single balanced pair of backticks, and build both start-anchored patterns (`_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` and `_TAG_AT_START_RE`) from it. This fits because every deterministic consumer already imports from this one module, so one change makes all of them agree by construction, and keeping the alternation non-capturing preserves the single capture group that `decide_ops` `.findall()` relies on. Both spellings (`non-codebase` and the `operator-attested` alias) go through the same alternation, so they cannot diverge. Rules that stay unchanged: the tag still counts only at the start of the checkbox text; a mention of the tag later in the line, in a code span or not, is still not a tag; an unbalanced single backtick is not accepted; matching stays case-insensitive and exact on the hyphenated tokens.

Then align the surfaces that describe the tag:

- The two LLM prompts (`completion_verifier.md`, `plan_review_evidence_kind.md`) state that the tag may be written bare or in backticks and counts the same either way, so the verifier's classification matches the deterministic matcher.
- The close-refusal message in `txn.py` names the exact accepted form, `- [ ] [non-codebase] <criterion>`, and says the tag may also be written in backticks.
- The misplaced-tag coaching (`misplaced_tag_issues`) and the close-precheck misplaced note (`_misplaced_tag_note`) keep their bare-form examples, which remain accepted.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` (AC-checkbox precheck section) records that the backticked form is accepted.

`completion_reconcile.py`, `det_advisory.py`, and `coach_moves.py` already show the bare form or mention the tag in prose only, so their text needs no change; the guidance-example test below proves their examples are accepted.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` — shared tag-form fragment; widened `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` and `_TAG_AT_START_RE`; comments updated.
- `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` — close-refusal message states the exact accepted form.
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md` — tag contract accepts the backticked form.
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_evidence_kind.md` — tag contract accepts the backticked form.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — precheck section records the backticked form.
- `tests/unit/test_non_codebase_backticked_tag.py` — new regression tests (below).

## Testing

New module `tests/unit/test_non_codebase_backticked_tag.py`, written first and observed failing before the fix:

- Happy path: backticked and bare forms of both spellings, under `- [ ]` and `- [x]`, match `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` with the same captured criterion text; `decide_ops.operator_attested_ac_texts` returns the same text for both.
- Close precheck: `ensure_ac_boxes_checked` (called with `ticket_state=`) does not raise for an unchecked backticked-tag item, and still raises for an untagged unchecked item.
- Attested handling of a ticked box: `det_measurement_provenance.provenance_gaps` reports a ticked backticked-tag item that lacks a `provenance:` line, and `ensure_attested_items_valid` refuses it; `det_attestation_launder.laundering_gaps` reports a ticked backticked-tag item citing a test path.
- DET checks: `operator_evidence_ac_gaps` treats a backticked-tag item as tagged; `misplaced_tag_lines` does not report a backticked tag at the start, and still reports a bare tag in the middle of the text.
- Edge / negative: an unbalanced backtick before the tag, a tag in a code span later in the line, a near-miss token, and a backticked tag with no criterion text do not match.
- Guidance examples: every `- [ ]` tag example extracted from `COMPLETION_REMEDIATION_GUIDANCE`, `misplaced_tag_issues` output, the `ensure_ac_boxes_checked` refusal message, and `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` matches `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE`.

Existing suites that cover these parsers (`tests/unit/test_non_codebase_tag.py`, `tests/unit/test_misplaced_noncodebase_tag_ef13.py`, `tests/unit/test_attested_close_guard.py`, `tests/unit/test_det_measurement_provenance.py`, `tests/unit/test_det_attestation_launder.py`, `tests/unit/test_evidence_kind_criterion.py`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_ac_checkbox_precheck.py`) must stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test asserts the backticked form and the bare form of `[non-codebase]` resolve the same way under `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` (same captured criterion text) for both `- [ ]` and `- [x]` checkboxes; verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_non_codebase_backticked_tag.py`.
- [ ] The same resolution applies to the `[operator-attested]` compatibility alias, so the two spellings cannot diverge; verified by parametrized cases in `tests/unit/test_non_codebase_backticked_tag.py`.
- [ ] A test asserts `ensure_ac_boxes_checked` does not refuse a close for an unchecked item tagged in either accepted form, and still refuses an untagged unchecked item; verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_non_codebase_backticked_tag.py`.
- [ ] A ticked box with a backticked tag is handled as an attested criterion, not an ordinary one: `provenance_gaps` and `laundering_gaps` report it, and `ensure_attested_items_valid` refuses it when its provenance line is missing; verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_non_codebase_backticked_tag.py`.
- [ ] The plan-review DET checks agree with the matcher: `operator_evidence_ac_gaps` treats a backticked-tag item as tagged, `misplaced_tag_lines` does not report a backticked tag at the start, and `operator_attested_ac_texts` returns its criterion text; verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_non_codebase_backticked_tag.py`.
- [ ] An unbalanced backtick, a tag inside a later code span, a near-miss token, and an empty criterion still do not match; verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_non_codebase_backticked_tag.py`.
- [ ] Every guidance example of the tag in `completion_reconcile.py`, `det_operator_attested.py`, the `txn.py` close-refusal message, and `writing-a-passing-plan.md` is accepted by the matcher; verified by the guidance-example test in `tests/unit/test_non_codebase_backticked_tag.py`.
- [ ] The completion-verifier and evidence-kind prompts state that the backticked tag counts the same as the bare tag; verified by `git grep -n "backtick" -- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_evidence_kind.md` returning a hit in each file.
- [ ] The close-refusal message in `txn.py` states the exact accepted form `- [ ] [non-codebase] <criterion>` rather than an untagged description of it; verified by a message assertion in `tests/unit/test_non_codebase_backticked_tag.py`.
- [ ] The existing tag suites listed under Testing stay green and `make verify` passes; verified by running `make verify` in the worktree before push.

## Provenance

Found while closing `f10f-c24a-3cfa-449e`. The regex behaviour above was measured by importing `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` and matching both forms, not inferred from reading it.
